subject: Next steps: hyperscaler comparison & OpenAI-compat migration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@zephyrai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: hyperscaler comparison & OpenAI-compat migration

Hi Emma — great to meet today, thanks for the deep dive. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of today's discovery
- Primary goal: move inference off embedded vendor endpoints and consolidate on a single runtime that gives predictable latency + lower unit cost.
- Key constraints: SOC2 compliance, VPC requirement for some workloads, 99th pct latency target of < 220ms for short chat flows, and support for an OpenAI-compatible API to minimize client changes.

2) What you asked for (action items)
- Hyperscaler comparison: side-by-side on latency/cost model vs GCP Vertex and AWS Bedrock for your 700k tokens/month baseline.
- Proof of compatibility: a small test harness that shows OpenAI-compatible calls (chat/completions/embeddings) with identical prompts and token accounting.
- SDK migration plan: sample code for swapping from openai-python to Redwood SDK with minimal changes and feature parity notes.

I've attached a compact matrix (hyperscaler-comparison-matrix.xlsx) with the high-level differentiation we discussed, and a starter SDK migration doc.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- I will share the test harness and migration notes with your engineering team by EOD Nov 4.
- Emma: please share 2-3 representative prompt sets (short chat, single-turn generation, and 512-dim embedding batch) and a preferred latency/load profile (concurrency + QPS).
- Let's schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineers and our solutions team — are you available Thurs 11/5 10:00am PT?

If that all looks right I'll loop in Karthik (SE) and Rishi (Solutions) to design the compatibility runbooks.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0122
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hyperscaler-comparison-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_sdk_migration_notes.md (md)

From: Emma Zhao <emma@zephyrai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: hyperscaler comparison & OpenAI-compat migration

Thanks Ben — the recap looks good and thanks for the matrix. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Prompts: attaching two anonymized prompt sets (chat_short_prompts.txt, long_gen_prompts.txt) and an embeddings.csv with 120 sample vectors. Please keep them internal.
- Latency/load profile: our target is 99th <= 220ms at 200 concurrent users with a steady-state of ~80 QPS for short-chat flows. We can simulate ramp to 300 QPS for stress runs.
- Cost comparison: can you include an apples-to-apples charge model (token counting rules + packaging/egress assumptions) for GCP/AWS/Redwood so we can model monthly spend for our 700k token baseline and 3x growth scenario?

Technical ask: we have some proprietary prompt-wrapping logic (pre/post processing) in our app. Please include sample code for 1) callouts to external tools (tool calls) and 2) streaming responses so we can verify SDK parity.

We are available for the technical deep-dive Thurs 11/5 10:00am PT — I'll invite our lead infra (procurement might join later).

--
Emma Zhao
Head of AI Platforms, Zephyr AI
emma@zephyrai.com

Attachments: chat_short_prompts.txt (txt), long_gen_prompts.txt (txt), embeddings.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Folks — forwarding Emma's asks and our matrix. High-level asks we need to cover before Thurs deep-dive: 

A) Compatibility runbook (Karthik lead)
- Create a small harness that takes Emma's prompt sets and performs: chat completion (streaming), single-turn generation, and batch embeddings.
- Verify token accounting parity vs OpenAI (prompt+completion counting, streaming accounting).
- Run against: Redwood-hosted (t1-small), GCP Vertex (n1 equivalency), and an OpenAI endpoint if possible. Collate latency percentiles and cost per 1k tokens.

B) SDK migration doc & sample diff (Rishi lead)
- Provide before/after snippets: openai.ChatCompletion.create -> redwood.chat.create (or equivalent) showing streaming and tool-calls.
- Highlight breaking differences (auth headers, model naming, response fields) and pragmatic shim suggestions.

C) Deliverables + timeline
- Compatibility harness + initial run results: target Fri 11/6 EOD (we can show preliminary numbers Thu during the deep-dive).
- SDK migration notes + code samples: Thurs 11/5 EOD.

Notes: Marissa — can you add cost modeling assumptions to the hyperscaler matrix (egress, reserved capacity multipliers)?

Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Next steps: hyperscaler comparison & OpenAI-compat migration

Thanks Ben — following up with the technical checklist and proposed plan. I took Emma's prompt sets and sketched the compatibility test steps below.

1) Test harness (code + infra)- Repo: internal stub (link in drive) with three runners: chat_stream_runner, gen_runner, embed_batch_runner.- Runtime targets: Redwood-hosted (dev tier), GCP Vertex (broad CPU/GPU mix), OpenAI (public).- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens in/out, bytes egress.

2) API compatibility checks- Authentication: test both API key header and token-based exchange.- Streaming: verify chunk boundaries map to expected token counts (our streaming framing vs OpenAI event streams).- Tool-calls: emulate a simple tool-call (weather lookup) and verify function-calling payload round-trip.

3) Data for cost model- We will instrument the harness to output token accounting in the standard OpenAI counting format. Marissa: please confirm cost multipliers for reserved capacity vs on-demand pricing so we can compute a 12-month TCO.

4) Timeline and risks- Thurs 11/5: technical deep-dive (we'll bring preliminary harness & plan).- Fri 11/6 EOD: first-pass runs and CSV outputs.- Risk: latency at p99 may vary significantly when comparing GPU-optimized Redwood runtime vs hyperscaler managed endpoints; we'll include 95% confidence intervals.

5) Deliverables (artifacts)
- compat-test-harness.tar.gz (script + sample infra Terraform),
- CSVs: latency_token_runs_<provider>.csv,
- redwood_sdk_migration_notes.md (diff + shims)

Next actions for Emma: confirm the Thurs time and share any additional prompts or the exact concurrency profile if different from the stated 200 concurrent users.

I'll prep the harness and share the drive link before the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments planned: compat-test-harness.tar.gz, redwood_sdk_migration_notes.md
